builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ADTGuard: Adaptive Depth-Time Safeguard for Streaming Inference in Large Language Models
summary: ADTGuard replaces post-hoc moderation and fixed-layer token-level guardrails by integrating safety evidence across depth and time at every token, using a causal router to select observation layers and refined token-level targets from response-level labels. It adds 16M trainable parameters and per-token latency, and requires training infrastructure to optimize the DTSD, CDR, and RTR components on safety benchmarks. Performance can fail when response-level labels provide weak supervision for precise risk onset, when the causal router selects suboptimal layers for out-of-distribution inputs, or when adversarial prefixes evade accumulated risk detection.
rationale: The method addresses a genuine production need for streaming safety with parameter efficiency suitable for a 24GB GPU, but its dependence on training and custom integration necessitates workload-specific validation before adoption.

claims.statement: ADTGuard replaces post-hoc moderation and fixed-layer token-level guardrails by integrating safety evidence across depth and time at every token, using a causal router to select observation layers and refined token-level targets from response-level labels. It adds 16M trainable parameters and per-token latency, and requires training infrastructure to optimize the DTSD, CDR, and RTR components on safety benchmarks. Performance can fail when response-level labels provide weak supervision for precise risk onset, when the causal router selects suboptimal layers for out-of-distribution inputs, or when adversarial prefixes evade accumulated risk detection.
Matches or surpasses state-of-the-art streaming safeguards with only 16M trainable parameters and competitive per-token latency.
